definition: bring oneself into favor through flattery or effort to please
memoryTip: In + graces: flattery to get into someone’s good graces.
correctPassage: Hoping for a promotion, the junior analyst tried to ingratiate herself with the partners by taking on thankless assignments.
wrongPassages: His decision to challenge the chair’s proposal in open session was an attempt to ingratiate himself with the committee.
She managed to ingratiate the rival department by blocking every request for shared resources.
The envoy sought to ingratiate the host government by publicly dismissing its concerns.

definition: excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters
memoryTip: A garrulous guest pours a garbled river of endless small talk.
correctPassage: A garrulous seatmate turned the short flight into an unbroken stream of minor anecdotes.
wrongPassages: Editors preferred the garrulous brief because it cut every unnecessary detail.
The garrulous archivist rarely spoke and answered questions only in writing.
Colleagues valued her garrulous manner for how quickly she moved past small talk.

memoryTip: Fervor on fire — fervid means passion running hot.
correctPassage: Fervid supporters of the reform filled the hearing room hours before the session began.
wrongPassages: His fervid reaction to the announcement was a shrug and a request to adjourn.
Critics called the novel fervid for its cool detachment and carefully understated tone.
The committee’s fervid endorsement consisted of polite silence and no further comment.

memoryTip: Exigent = emergency-urgent — it demands attention now.
correctPassage: Auditors described the funding shortfall as exigent, prompting the board to meet that evening.
wrongPassages: Because the request was exigent, staff were told they could respond whenever convenient.
He filed the exigent forms several months late with no sense of urgency.
The optional survey was labeled exigent so employees would feel free to ignore it.

definition: understood by only a small specialist group
memoryTip: Eso-teric: for the inner circle only — specialist knowledge.
correctPassage: The paper’s esoteric methodology limited its readership to specialists in the field.
wrongPassages: The esoteric handbook became required reading in nearly every introductory course.
She favored esoteric explanations because they used only everyday vocabulary.
Networks chose esoteric programming precisely for its broad popular appeal.
